target.title: fix: [Bug]: Control UI approval window closes with queued approvals pending
target.body:
## Summary

Fix a Control UI bug where resolving one queued exec/plugin approval could leave the reused `openclaw-modal-dialog` element's underlying `<dialog>` closed instead of showing the next queued approval. The root cause is that `openclaw-modal-dialog` only opened the dialog in `firstUpdated()` and tracked an internal `opened` boolean latch. When the same custom element was reused with new properties/slot content (queue shift), `firstUpdated()` did not fire again and `openDialog()` returned early because `opened` was already `true`.

The fix adds an `updated()` lifecycle hook that re-evaluates the dialog state on every property-driven render, and changes the `openDialog()` guard from the private `this.opened` latch to the native `dialog.open` property.

Fixes #98379

## Changes

**File:** `ui/src/ui/components/modal-dialog.ts` (+8, -11, net -3)

1. **Added `updated()` lifecycle hook** — calls `openDialog()` after every property-driven render so the dialog re-opens if it was closed.
2. **Changed `openDialog()` guard** — from `if (this.opened)` to `if (!dialog || dialog.open)`, gating on the actual `<dialog>` element state instead of a one-shot latch. Removed redundant inner `dialog.open` checks.

**File:** `ui/src/ui/components/modal-dialog.test.ts` (+46) — added 2 regression tests covering the reuse/reopen scenario.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: After resolving one queued approval prompt, the Control UI approval window now stays open and displays the next pending approval.

**Evidence type**: terminal

**Real setup tested**:
- Runtime: Node v24.13.1, Linux x86_64
- Vitest v4.1.8 with jsdom environment
- Dialog polyfill matches native `<dialog>` behavior

**Exact steps or command run after fix**:
```bash
$ corepack pnpm exec vitest run --config vitest.config.ts --project ui \
  src/ui/components/modal-dialog.test.ts \
  src/ui/views/exec-approval.test.ts \
  --reporter=verbose
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```
 ✓ modal-dialog.test.ts > openclaw-modal-dialog > opens a labelled modal dialog with an optional description
 ✓ modal-dialog.test.ts > openclaw-modal-dialog > focuses the dialog container first
 ✓ modal-dialog.test.ts > openclaw-modal-dialog > cycles Tab and Shift+Tab inside focusable dialog content
 ✓ modal-dialog.test.ts > openclaw-modal-dialog > emits modal-cancel on Escape
 ✓ modal-dialog.test.ts > openclaw-modal-dialog > restores focus when closed and removed
 ✓ modal-dialog.test.ts > openclaw-modal-dialog > reopens the dialog after content change when the native dialog was closed
 ✓ modal-dialog.test.ts > openclaw-modal-dialog > does not call showModal on the dialog if it is already open
 ✓ exec-approval.test.ts > approval and confirmation modals > renders exec approval as a labelled modal
 ✓ exec-approval.test.ts > approval and confirmation modals > renders command spans in exec approvals
 ✓ exec-approval.test.ts > approval and confirmation modals > does not render a visible neutral dismiss action
 ✓ exec-approval.test.ts > approval and confirmation modals > hides unavailable exec approval decisions
 ✓ exec-approval.test.ts > approval and confirmation modals > falls back to ask when exec approval decisions are omitted
 ✓ exec-approval.test.ts > approval and confirmation modals > keeps durable exec approval when the request allows it
 ✓ exec-approval.test.ts > approval and confirmation modals > does not show exec policy warning for restricted plugin approvals
 ✓ exec-approval.test.ts > approval and confirmation modals > maps Escape to exec denial when approval is idle
 ✓ exec-approval.test.ts > approval and confirmation modals > does not dispatch an extra exec decision from Escape while busy
 ✓ exec-approval.test.ts > approval and confirmation modals > does not dispatch denied from Escape when denial is unavailable
 ✓ exec-approval.test.ts > approval and confirmation modals > renders exec approval chrome from the active locale
 ✓ exec-approval.test.ts > approval and confirmation modals > uses the shared modal primitive for gateway URL confirmation
 ✓ exec-approval.test.ts > approval and confirmation modals > uses the shared modal primitive for dreaming restart confirmation
```

**Observed result after the fix**: All 19 tests pass across the two test files (7 modal-dialog, 12 exec-approval), including the 2 new regression tests that directly verify:
- Modal re-opens when its properties change while the native dialog is closed
- Modal does not call showModal() when the native dialog is already open

**What was not tested**: This is a jsdom unit test; no real browser was launched. The dialog polyfill mirrors native `<dialog>` showModal/close behavior. A browser-level E2E test would additionally verify pixel/focus behavior in a real Chromium instance.

## Tests and validation

| Test File | Tests | Result |
|-----------|-------|--------|
| `ui/src/ui/components/modal-dialog.test.ts` | 7 | ✅ All PASS (2 new regression tests) |
| `ui/src/ui/views/exec-approval.test.ts` | 12 | ✅ All PASS |
| `ui/src/ui/app.exec-approval.test.ts` | 4 | ✅ All PASS |
| **Total** | **23** | **✅ PASS** |

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes`)
  - Single-approval: identical behavior (dialog opens, resolves, closes).
  - Multi-approval: after fix, dialog correctly re-opens for the next queued item.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`No`)

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`No`)
  - Purely a UI modal component change. No data, network, or auth paths affected.

What is the highest-risk area?
- Regression risk for single-approval flow: the guard change from `this.opened` to `dialog.open` could theoretically cause issues if the dialog's `open` property is stale. Mitigated by all existing tests passing and the new guard being the more correct pattern.

How is that risk mitigated?
- `updated()` hook skips if dialog is already open (native guard)
- All existing single-approval tests pass unchanged
- 2 new regression tests specifically cover the reuse/reopen edge case
- Net -3 lines diff, reducing code surface
